thread:
jamie: Heads-up: noticed inconsistency between CLI exit codes in the ruby gem and the other SDK CLIs. Our sampleapp CI expects 1 for failures but the ruby CLI returns 2 on auth errors. Repro: run bin/redwood-cli without token -> exit 2

maria: oof, thanks for flagging. Is this breaking CI or just local tooling?

jamie: Breaking a couple integration jobs in sampleapp pipeline that assert exit_code == 1 for failures. Local devs hit it too.

siva: I can take a look. Quick Q: do we have an exit-code policy anywhere? I thought we agreed: 0 success, 1 generic failure, 2 usage/cli-parse issues.

natalie: go-client CLI returns 1 for any runtime error; node does the same. Ruby returning 2 seems to come from our rescue block in bin/redwood that calls exit(2) on AuthError.

jamie: here's the snippet that causes it:

```
begin
  run_cli
rescue AuthError
  puts "auth failed"
  exit(2)
end
```

Should we change auth -> exit(1) or remap semantics?

siva: I'd prefer standardizing: 0 success, 1 generic error (incl auth/runtime), 2 usage/flag/arg parsing errors. That keeps 2 for optparse/Thor usage problems. Auth should be 1.

maria: agree. Also we should add a short test so CI catches regressions and update sampleapp scripts. Tiny change but wide surface.

natalie: I'll open a PR in ruby-sdk with a test asserting exit codes for simulated AuthError and for optparse parse failure. Can tag folks for quick review.

jamie: I'll review the PR. Also updating sampleapp CI to assert exit != 0 for now so it doesn't flake while change lands.

maria: thanks — can we also add a short note in devex docs about CLI exit semantics so integrators know what to expect? Might save others from similar flakes. :memo:
